messages.subject: Collaborative Cross Mice and R/qtl2
parts:
Hello, I'm new to the R/qtl2 Google group, and I had emailed Dr. Broman with a few questions about a QTL study involving Collaborative Cross mice, which he kindly answered. However, these questions may be helpful to a larger audience, so I would like to post them here as well. Thanks! Chris

===========================================================

Q1: What type of cross applies for CC mice? My guess is "hs" (8-way heterogeneous stock), because the CC mice derive from an original eight inbred strains, but I don't know for sure.

A1: For the CC, use "risib8", for 8-way recombinant inbred lines by sibling mating. HS is a heterozygous population, while with the CC we assume they're homozygous everyone.

===========================================================

Q2: Do I need the phenotype data for each individual CC mouse in the study, or should I average the phenotypes for all mice of the same CC strain?

A2: The easiest way to do the analysis is with strain means. The measurements on individual mice are really useful for learning about heritability of the trait, and there's some discussion about taking into account the within-strain variance, but I'd start with strain means.

===========================================================

Q3: Relatedly, do I need to experimentally measure the genotype markers present within each individual mouse, or does the qtl2 package know the markers already given the CC strain number?

A3. qtl2 doesn't have built-in data for the CC, but there is CC data in R/qtl2 format at the qtl2data repository, https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data/tree/main/CC
There's also data available from the jackson lab resource page on DO/CC:
https://www.jax.org/research-and-faculty/genetic-diversity-initiative/tools-data/diversity-outbred-reference-data
